reading.body:
CoreSite LA2 publishes 432,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, this campus cannot be ranked among the five California facilities on this site that do publish megawatts, and no capacity translation into racks or accelerators is possible without inventing a figure the operator has not released. What the square footage does establish is that the floor area is substantial: 432,000 square feet of technical space places LA2 among the larger footprints by area, though floor area and power capacity do not move in lockstep at AI training densities, so the number alone does not resolve the campus's power position.

The six certifications qualify the campus for specific workload categories in narrow terms. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for financially sensitive and operationally audited workloads. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 qualifies it for workloads requiring a certified information security management system. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for workloads aligned to US federal security controls. Together the set covers regulated industries, but the certifications say nothing about power density ceilings or GPU-class cooling readiness.

California has 103 mapped facilities on this site, of which only 5 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 170 MW across those five. LA2 does not appear in that five because it publishes no MW figure, placing it outside the ranked set entirely. Los Angeles is a major interconnection market, and a 432,000-square-foot footprint in downtown LA is a material physical presence, but whether LA2 is a meaningful node for AI scaling depends entirely on its power allocation, and that number is not published.
